units.translation: where I restored κελεύμασιν [commands] for κελεύσμασιν [commands]; M preserved this reading.
where in the apograph κελεύσματος [of a command].
I have come at the command of Loxias.
they struck the deep brine at the word of command
I will surely command and call upon you
How do you bid me practice wickedness?
I will speak, since you command
commanding him to cross this danger
How then does he bid him come equipped?
he bids him bring spear-bearing attendants
Out, I command you, go quickly from this house
may Zeus, father of the Olympians, not command (thus Hermann for κελεύσει [will command])
now I bid them cast their vote according to their judgment
I bid you fear my oracles and those of Zeus
I command you to release by force
I bid you go to the double-turning ship
to bring a ship to land
to bring a ship to land
having landed (thus Auratus for κελσάντων [of those who landed]) on the leafy shores of Simois, following the invisible track of the oars
having landed on the ship-traversed shores
he ordained to flee unhindered through the sea wave, and to land on the land of Argos
Who expected that this unexpected flight would land (κέλσειεν [would land] M) at Argos?
Where must you land to see an end of these toils?
What Fury is this you bid (κέλη [you bid] M) raise her cry against the house?
the whole city groans at the absence of men
the great city of Susa empty of men
never yet has a day without hunting sent Actaeon home rich in empty toil
having emptied the whole expanse of the mainland
may a plague of men never empty this city
himself by his own empty-minded counsels
a sting of the tongue (λύσσης [of madness] Lobeck on Soph. Aj. p. 203, second ed.), I mean the arrow of a scorpion
and with sting-wounding pains (thus Erfurdt for κεντροδαλήτοις [sting-wounding]) the maenad of Hera
where Hermann has κεντροις - - φοιταλέοις [with maddening stings] for κέντροισι φοιταλέοισιν [with maddening stings]. Others κεντρώμασιν φοιταλέοις [with maddening stings].
will you not stretch your leg against the goads?
she wastes me, anointing me with maddening stings
fears that he will tear my soul with a two-edged goad
shame – he struck like a charioteer, piercing him with the goad
where is there so great a goad as to commit matricide?
what sound, what divine or mortal scent is this, or is it mixed?
of the horn used as a drinking cup
with silver-wrought horns fitted with golden mouthpieces
first the right well-ordered wing led in order
According to Arcadius p. 35, 19 κεραστίς [horned] is oxytone.
and horned, as you see, anointed with a sharp-mouthed gadfly
